## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** No issue found in the reviewed scope. On Hyprland 0.56.2 (the version Arch currently packages), both PiP rules now open at the intended 40px margin regardless of the client's initial size. The author's premise matches the Hyprland source.

### Why `window_w` does not reflect `size` on 0.56.2

On first floating map, Hyprland 0.56.2 evaluates the `size` rule before `move`. It stores the computed size in the window geometry, but writes it to the position animation instead of the size animation. `window_w`/`window_h` read the size animation, so `move` still sees the client's initial size:

```text
CDefaultFloatingAlgorithm::newTarget (src/layout/algorithm/floating/default/DefaultFloatingAlgorithm.cpp, v0.56.2)
  size animation  <- client initial size (e.g. 200x112)
  size rule       -> 600x338 stored in geometry; positionAnimation()->setValueAndWarp(size)
  move rule       -> window_w / window_h = size animation goal = 200x112
```

Upstream treats this as a regression from hyprwm/Hyprland@723870337 and fixed it on `main` in hyprwm/Hyprland#16150 (merged 2026-09-12). No tagged release includes the fix yet. The inlined values give the same placement before and after that fix.

**Verified:** placement on a 1440x900 logical monitor with a 200x112 initial client (arithmetic model driven by the real `pip.lua` rules and the variable bindings in the Hyprland source; not a compositor run):

| Rule | Base (`window_w`/`window_h`) | This PR (inlined 600/338) |
|---|---|---|
| Generic PiP x | 1200, right edge 1800 (360 off-screen) | 800, right edge 1400 (40 margin) |
| Meet PiP y | 748, bottom edge 1086 (186 off-screen) | 522, bottom edge 860 (40 margin) |

On base, any client narrower than 560 overhangs by `560 - width` on every monitor size, which matches the description's note that the overflow is roughly the same on large displays. With the PR, the right margin is 40 logical px across the scale and monitor sizes modelled. Scaling, multi-monitor offsets and the bar area behave as on base.

**Verified:** `test/shell.d/pip-window-rules-test.sh` passes on this PR and fails when run against the base `pip.lua`, reporting both `window_w`/`window_h` move lines.

**Optional test improvement:** two diagnostic mutations still pass the test: changing both `size` values to 640x360 while leaving `move` at 600/338, and changing only the Meet `move` x to `(monitor_w-640-40)`. The `grep -F` checks match anywhere in the file, so one correct rule satisfies them for both. Matching each rule's full `move = { ... }` line, as `test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh` does for the webcam overlay, would catch the second case. A check that each `move` uses its rule's `size` would catch the first.

**Optional:** the new `pip.lua` comment describes the behaviour as general Hyprland semantics. Noting that it works around an upstream regression (hyprwm/Hyprland#16150) would tell future maintainers why the values are inlined and that they stay correct after the fix.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR, `default/hypr/helpers.lua`, `default/hypr/apps/webcam-overlay.lua`, and Hyprland v0.56.2 source plus the upstream fix commit. The new test ran in an isolated sandbox against head, base and diagnostic mutations. Placement figures come from a source-derived arithmetic model. No Hyprland session, browser PiP window or live display was used, so the reported Chromium initial size and the manual 1440x900 test were not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
